market_regime: Late-cycle, sticky-inflation regime: CPI at a 3-year high, oil up ~10% on war/Hormuz risk, 10Y near 5%, and the Fed expected to hike again in December rather than cut. Leadership has rotated hard into defensives and energy while Technology and Communication momentum rolls over amid renewed AI-capex 'gut check' anxiety and a VIX up 24% on the month.

themes.name: Energy & oil-levered inflation beneficiaries
themes.thesis: Energy is the top sector on both 1m (+10.8%) and 3m (+21.2%), driven by WTI +9-10% on war-related supply risk (Strait of Hormuz chatter) and persistent inflation. With the Fed leaning hawkish on energy-driven inflation, integrated producers, E&Ps and services carry the strongest trend in the tape.

themes.name: Defensive consumer staples
themes.thesis: Classic late-cycle rotation: Staples +8.0%/1m and +9.3%/3m as recession-risk questions dominate advisor conversations and Goldman flags defensive names for a slowing economy. Stable cash flows and pricing power hold up as discretionary/tech leadership fades.

themes.name: Health care leadership
themes.thesis: Health Care is the 3m leader at +23.5% and +5.5% on the month, combining defensive earnings with its own momentum as capital exits high-multiple tech. Large-cap pharma and managed care offer durable demand independent of the rate cycle.

themes.name: Utilities & power for AI/electrification
themes.thesis: Utilities +8.1%/1m reflect both defensive rotation and a structural power-demand story: semiconductor industry electricity use hit a record and AI data-center capex remains enormous even as equity enthusiasm wobbles. Regulated utilities and independent power producers monetize the grid/power bottleneck with less direct AI-valuation risk.

avoid.what: Mega-cap technology and communication services (QQQ, high-multiple AI/software)
avoid.reason: Worst sectors: Tech -5.9%/1m, Comm -7.4%/1m, with renewed AI-capex 'gut check' fears, hyperscaler debt warnings, and CoreWeave stress. Momentum is firmly negative and valuations are rate-sensitive into a hawkish Fed.

avoid.what: Long-duration bond proxies and rate-sensitive REITs
avoid.reason: 10Y near 5% and a December hike expected; the Fed cut has been pushed to late 2026, pressuring long-duration and leveraged real estate.
Gold is down -6.8%/1m and -11.3%/3m despite inflation, showing a broken near-term trend as real yields and the dollar firm.
Washington's robot curbs could cut US humanoid robotics revenue by ~58% via lost China access; hype-cycle risk and policy headwinds make the theme untradeable on fundamentals right now.
Industrials are lagging (-2.5%/1m, -5.0%/3m) amid tariff disruption and slowing-growth signals, with no positive momentum confirmation.
